assumptions: Target users (college students) have regular access to a desktop or laptop computer during their daily study routine.
The 20 trial users can be easily reached and assisted with email registration issues if needed.
The exam syllabus and materials are already sourced by the users themselves; the tool acts only as a planner, not a content provider.
A weekly granularity is sufficient for tracking progress without requiring hourly schedules in the MVP.
A 2-week continuous task completion rate is a reliable early indicator of long-term product value.
candidates: Predefined weekly milestones for major public subjects (Mathematics I/II/III, English I/II, Political Theory) to automate task generation.
Syllabus templates for user-defined custom professional subjects.
Task priority tags (High, Medium, Low) to help users prioritize when behind schedule.
Simple calendar export (ICS format) for WeChat, Apple Calendar, or Outlook.
confirmed: Targeted at Chinese postgraduate entrance exam (考研) candidates.
Language support: Chinese (Simplified) only.
Platform support: Desktop web browsers only.
Onboarding inputs: Exam date, chosen subjects, weekly study hours, and current foundation level.
Core engine: System automatically generates a weekly-based review plan.
Core feature: Generated plan must be adjustable by the user.
Homepage components: Current week's tasks, weekly completion progress, and exam countdown.
Task detail options: Mark as completed, postpone (延后), or split (拆分).
Data storage: Email registration/login with cloud database synchronization.
UI/UX theme: Quiet, encouraging, professional, combining calendar and to-do lists.
Out of MVP Scope: Social features, course marketplace, AI chat, and mobile application/web version.
Validation strategy: Test with 20 students, success measured by the proportion of students who continuously complete tasks for two weeks.
conflicts: User Demographics vs. Authentication Choice: Email registration is chosen for ease of MVP development, but Chinese college students heavily prefer WeChat/SMS logins, which may affect trial onboarding completion.

Desktop Only vs. Library Study Habit: 考研 students spend most of their study time in libraries or study rooms where opening a laptop just to check off a task is inconvenient compared to checking it on a mobile screen.

gaps.reason: While a full mobile app is excluded from MVP, complete lack of mobile accessibility might prevent students from logging tasks completed while studying in libraries.

gaps.reason: The generation logic for the plans is undefined. If the system doesn't know the syllabus of the subjects, it cannot generate tasks.

questions.reason: In 考研, falling behind schedule is extremely common. The mechanism for handling postponed tasks will dictate the tone of the UI and the complexity of the backend.
questions.recommendation: Move postponed tasks to a 'Backlog' or 'Inbox' for manual redistribution, showing a gentle warning if the backlog grows too large.
questions.recommendation_reason: Automatically recalculating and shifting the entire plan can be technically complex and psychologically overwhelming for the user. A backlog queue gives them control to manually reschedule when they feel ready.

questions.question: What authentication method should be used for the 20-student trial?
questions.reason: While email is simple to implement, WeChat login or SMS login is the standard in China and has much higher completion rates.
questions.recommendation: Stick to Email registration for the 20-student MVP to bypass Chinese regulatory/corporate verification, adding direct onboarding support.
questions.recommendation_reason: For a private trial of 20 hand-picked students, we can coordinate with them directly and assist with any setup issues, avoiding the need for formal corporate registration.

risks: Device Disconnect Risk (High): Students study in libraries where they might not open a laptop. Lacking a mobile-friendly view to log tasks could lead to under-reporting and artificial validation failure.

Onboarding/Setup Friction (Medium): If the system cannot generate realistic tasks immediately, manually setting up a 6-month schedule on day one will cause users to drop out before the 2-week trial starts.
Login Friction (Medium): Chinese college students rarely check email, leading to forgotten passwords, missed verification links, and activation drop-offs.
Rescheduling Burnout (Medium): Continuous postponement without a smart consolidation logic will lead to an overwhelming backlog, making the UI feel stressful rather than quiet.

confirmed: Targeted at Chinese postgraduate entrance exam (考研) candidates.
Language support: Chinese (Simplified) only.
Platform support: Desktop web browsers only.
Onboarding inputs: Exam date, chosen subjects, weekly study hours, and current foundation level.
Core engine: System automatically generates a weekly-based review plan.
Core feature: Generated plan must be adjustable by the user.
Homepage components: Current week's tasks, weekly completion progress, and exam countdown.
Task detail options: Mark as completed, postpone (延后), or split (拆分).
Data storage: Email registration/login with cloud database synchronization.
UI/UX theme: Quiet, encouraging, professional, combining calendar and to-do lists.
Out of MVP Scope: Social features, course marketplace, AI chat, and mobile application/web version.
Validation strategy: Test with 20 students, success measured by the proportion of students who continuously complete tasks for two weeks.
conflicts: User Demographics vs. Authentication Choice: Email registration is chosen for ease of MVP development, but Chinese college students heavily prefer WeChat/SMS logins, which may affect trial onboarding completion.

Desktop Only vs. Library Study Habit: 考研 students spend most of their study time in libraries or study rooms where opening a laptop just to check off a task is inconvenient compared to checking it on a mobile screen.

questions.question: How should the system generate the initial study plan for the MVP?
questions.reason: Generating a high-quality study plan requires mapping out all subjects. Since AI is out of scope, we need a simple but effective way to populate tasks.
questions.recommendation: Predefine standard weekly milestones for common public subjects (Math, English, Politics), and let users manually enter tasks for professional subjects.
questions.recommendation_reason: This keeps the MVP scope small while still offering immediate value for the subjects that 90%+ of candidates take, avoiding the need to pre-build databases for hundreds of specialized professional courses.

options.impact: Simple to implement, gives users full control, and prevents compounding stress.
options.label: (Recommended) Move postponed tasks to a 'Backlog' or 'Inbox' for manual redistribution, showing a gentle warning if the backlog grows too large.

options.impact: Keeps the plan realistic but will eventually push the target date past the fixed exam date, rendering the plan invalid.
options.label: Automatically shift all subsequent tasks down the timeline, extending the overall plan length.

options.impact: Keeps the target date fixed, but incrementally increases the weekly study load, which can lead to burnout.
options.label: Distribute the postponed hours proportionally across all remaining weeks.

questions.question: How should the system handle rescheduled (postponed) tasks?
questions.reason: In 考研, falling behind schedule is extremely common. The mechanism for handling postponed tasks will dictate the tone of the UI and the complexity of the backend.
questions.recommendation: Move postponed tasks to a 'Backlog' or 'Inbox' for manual redistribution, showing a gentle warning if the backlog grows too large.
questions.recommendation_reason: Automatically recalculating and shifting the entire plan can be technically complex and psychologically overwhelming for the user. A backlog queue gives them control to manually reschedule when they feel ready.

options.impact: Saves weeks of administrative setup time, though slightly higher friction for users.

options.impact: Seamless user experience, but requires a registered Chinese enterprise and WeChat developer account verification.
options.label: Integrate WeChat scan-to-login, accepting the overhead of registering a corporate developer account.

options.impact: Very common and low friction, but requires real-name registration with an SMS provider and is prone to spam/cost issues.
options.label: Use SMS code verification login.

questions.question: What authentication method should be used for the 20-student trial?
questions.reason: While email is simple to implement, WeChat login or SMS login is the standard in China and has much higher completion rates.
questions.recommendation: Stick to Email registration for the 20-student MVP to bypass Chinese regulatory/corporate verification, adding direct onboarding support.
questions.recommendation_reason: For a private trial of 20 hand-picked students, we can coordinate with them directly and assist with any setup issues, avoiding the need for formal corporate registration.

risks: Device Disconnect Risk (High): Students study in libraries where they might not open a laptop. Lacking a mobile-friendly view to log tasks could lead to under-reporting and artificial validation failure.

Onboarding/Setup Friction (Medium): If the system cannot generate realistic tasks immediately, manually setting up a 6-month schedule on day one will cause users to drop out before the 2-week trial starts.
Login Friction (Medium): Chinese college students rarely check email, leading to forgotten passwords, missed verification links, and activation drop-offs.
Rescheduling Burnout (Medium): Continuous postponement without a smart consolidation logic will lead to an overwhelming backlog, making the UI feel stressful rather than quiet.
unknowns: The target threshold for the validation metric (what percentage of the 20 students completing 2 weeks constitutes a success?).
The specific professional subjects required by the 20 trial users.
